old_problem: The same errorlocation values that adjacent GMI rows define as IOD/CCD are relabeled Socket1/Socket0 here, so the literal selector cannot prove inter-socket direction; the link is also a placeholder.
disposition_reason: A safe parameterized test still needs to know which endpoint a command selects. Here the proprietary errorlocation field is internally inconsistent across adjacent source rows and determines socket/direction coverage, not just a runtime ID. ED-16 prohibits a fabric injection until AMD documentation resolves the selector and recovery. Because no public standard can define this tool-specific field, the case remains Pending/BLOCKED rather than guessing that two commands cover two sockets.
decision_basis: Read Reliability row 40, same-row AI fields, historical record 2443 and next pending row 41.
Preserved two-socket/directional xGMI CE coverage rather than counting two syntactic commands.
Compared adjacent GMI rows where errorlocation0/1 are labeled IOD/CCD and treated the conflict as material.
Required peer counters and link health in addition to a local corrected log.
No BIOS/HDT, link selection or injection action occurred.

test_case.test_name: xGMI3 correctable event by inter-socket direction
test_case.purpose: For every required xGMI direction, inject one correctable event at the documented source/remote endpoint and prove attributable CE reporting with healthy peer fabric.
required_package: Exact link and endpoint selectors for each required direction
Per-direction MCA/APEI/WHEA, counters and timeout oracle
BIOS/HDT, abort, OOB recovery and restoration
test_case.test_command: Do not substitute the placeholder or execute the source commands. After AMD authority defines errorlocation semantics, bind each enumerated link and direction, run one signed CE checkpoint under FAE control, correlate source and peer evidence/counters, verify link width/speed and restore all state.
test_case.expected_result: Each approved direction produces the correct attributable CE at the intended endpoint within the signed timeout while both peers and the coherent link remain healthy and all changes are restored.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS exists until errorlocation semantics prove which socket/endpoint/direction is exercised. Generic CE text, assumed Socket1/0 labels, a guessed link or two commands without peer attribution cannot pass.
safety_gate: Dedicated supported multi-socket SUT and independent OOB console.
No command until link, direction and selector meaning are authoritative.
One CE direction at a time; abort on wrong endpoint, UCE, storm, reset or link degradation.
Never auto-retry; preserve both peers' evidence.
expected_evidence: Approved xGMI topology and selector specification
Package hash/license and exact per-direction commands
Source/peer OS event and counter deltas
test_case.recovery: The platform owner must supply the fabric-specific recovery for wrong-target, degraded-link or escalation cases; execution remains blocked until that procedure and selector definition are versioned together.

source_conflict.reason: Socket labels conflict with adjacent IOD/CCD use of the same proprietary field, so command-to-direction identity is unresolved.

blocked.reason: Tool-specific endpoint semantics and fabric recovery cannot be derived from xGMI standards or safely parameterized as an opaque ID.
